headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and capability conflict: Claude Code can write shared repo files while social-auto-upload may consume them in automation flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can write repo files and use MCP; social-auto-upload runs in CLI/headless mode and may ingest files in its workflow. The pair shares filesystem-based interaction via Claude Code’s documented shared state, so attacker-controlled content in files can influence downstream parsing. This is plausible in default setups, though not proven by evidence.
conditions: IF agent_b reads files produced by agent_a without content provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents operate in the same workspace, file-mediated instruction smuggling becomes feasible.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Require provenance tags on any file passed from agent_a to agent_b.
Disable automatic parsing of agent_a-generated text as instructions.
Review shared-directory contents before agent_b consumes them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets like git credentials; social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads media. Because Claude Code shares state via filesystem and git, sensitive material can flow into files that the uploader may process or transmit. The leakage path is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a writes secrets or code context into shared files, agent_b may ingest them.
IF agent_b uploads files from the shared workspace, sensitive content can leave the host.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories.
Use a scrubber before any upload step.
Mount separate per-agent worktrees.
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while social-auto-upload operates on account files and can run multiple instances. Shared filesystem state creates a direct write-write conflict, and git mutations by agent_a can race with file-based account workflows in agent_b. This matches the rubric’s dangerous default overlap.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repo, concurrent writes can corrupt state.
IF agent_b stores account files in the same workspace, agent_a can overwrite them.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent.
Serialize git operations with a lock file.
Make agent_b’s account files read-only during agent_a runs.
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent execution.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, commands, and file edits that social-auto-upload could treat as operational input. If agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without verification, mistakes or fabricated instructions can cascade into uploads or account actions. The pathway exists, but the blast radius is bounded by the uploader’s task scope.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-produced files or commands as authoritative input, errors propagate.
IF agent_a emits malformed upload metadata, agent_b may execute the wrong action.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before uploads.
Validate schemas for any agent_a-produced metadata.
Reject free-form instructions from agent_a.
Log and diff all generated upload manifests.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and shell environment data, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media uploads. If account data or credentials are placed into shared files, retention and residency obligations can diverge between the two tools. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-mismatch risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated account data is stored in the shared workspace, retention policies may diverge.
IF credentials are copied into files processed by both agents, logging and retention controls may conflict.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files.
Apply a short retention policy to workspace artifacts.
Review logging settings for both tools.
Use separate credential stores per agent.
